Q: On a box plot, Q1 = 12, Q2 = 18, Q3 = 24. What is the IQR and what does the median's position tell you about skewness?

points.text: IQR = 24 – 12 = 12. The median (18) is exactly midway between Q1 and Q3, so the distribution is approximately symmetric.

questions.question: Q: A dataset has Q1 = 10, Q3 = 22. What are the outlier boundaries?

points.text: IQR = 12. Lower boundary = 10 – 1.5 × 12 = –8. Upper boundary = 22 + 1.5 × 12 = 40. Values below –8 or above 40 are outliers.

questions.question: Q: In a histogram, the total area of bars is 200 and one bar has an area of 40. What is the frequency for that bar?

points.text: Since area is proportional to frequency, the frequency is 40 (assuming the scale factor is 1, i.e. area = frequency).

questions.question: Q: Two box plots show the same median but different IQRs. What does this tell you?

points.text: The distributions have the same central value, but the one with the larger IQR has greater spread in the middle 50% of the data.

questions.question: Full-Mark Response The frequency table shows the times taken for 120 runners to complete a race. Draw a histogram. 0–10 min: frequency 15, 10–20 min: frequency 40, 20–40 min: frequency 45, 40–60 min: frequency 20 <div class="

points.text: Calculate frequency density for each class: 0–10: width = 10, FD = 15 ÷ 10 = 1.5 10–20: width = 10, FD = 40 ÷ 10 = 4.0 20–40: width = 20, FD = 45 ÷ 20 = 2.25 40–60: width = 20, FD = 20 ÷ 20 = 1.0 Draw the histogram with class boundaries on the x-axis (0, 10, 20, 40, 60) and frequency density on the y-axis. Each bar has no gap and its height equals the frequency density. Check: total area = (1.5 × 10) + (4.0 × 10) + (2.25 × 20) + (1.0 × 20) = 15 + 40 + 45 + 20 = 120
